chapterTitle: Chapter 13: Carboxylic Acids and Functional Derivatives
title: Chapter 13: Carboxylic Acids and Functional Derivatives
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: Carboxylic acids exist predominantly as cyclic dimers in non-polar solvents (like benzene) and in the vapor phase due to:

options.A: Two strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds formed between the carbonyl oxygen of one molecule and the hydroxyl hydrogen of the other

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids form eight-membered cyclic dimers held by two robust O-H···O=C hydrogen bonds, doubling the apparent molecular mass in benzene.

questions.question: Which of the following haloacetic acids is the strongest acid in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation: Three highly electronegative fluorine atoms exert an intense electron-withdrawing inductive (-I) effect, stabilizing the CF₃COO⁻ carboxylate anion.

questions.question: Carboxylic acids react with sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃) solution with brisk effervescence due to the evolution of:
questions.explanation: R-COOH + NaHCO₃ → R-COONa + H₂O + CO₂↑. This reaction distinguishes carboxylic acids from phenols (which generally do not liberate CO₂ from NaHCO₃).

questions.question: In Fischer Esterification, a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst (conc. H₂SO₄ or dry HCl). Isotopic tracer studies with ¹⁸O prove that:

options.A: The water molecule is formed from the -OH of the acid and the -H of the alcohol
options.B: The water molecule is formed from the -H of the acid and the -OH of the alcohol
options.D: The alcohol oxygen is converted to CO₂

questions.explanation: Labeling alcohol with ¹⁸O (R'-¹⁸OH) reveals that ¹⁸O ends up in the ester (R-CO-¹⁸OR'), proving that acyl-oxygen cleavage occurs and water derives from the carboxylic -OH.

questions.question: Which reagent is the most advantageous for converting a carboxylic acid into an acyl chloride (acid chloride, RCOCl) because both by-products are gaseous?
questions.explanation: R-COOH + SOCl₂ → R-COCl + SO₂↑ + HCl↑. The gaseous by-products bubble off, leaving pure acyl chloride.

questions.question: Among the carboxylic acid functional derivatives, what is the correct order of reactivity toward nucleophilic acyl substitution?

options.A: Acyl chloride > Acid anhydride > Ester > Acid amide
options.B: Acid amide > Ester > Acid anhydride > Acyl chloride
options.C: Ester > Acid amide > Acyl chloride > Acid anhydride
options.D: Acid anhydride > Acyl chloride > Ester > Acid amide

questions.explanation: Reactivity depends on leaving group ability: Cl⁻ (very weak base, best leaving group) > RCOO⁻ > RO⁻ > NH₂⁻ (strong base, poorest leaving group).

questions.question: When an acid amide is treated with bromine and concentrated aqueous KOH (Hofmann's Bromamide Degradation reaction), the organic product is:

options.A: A primary amine having one less carbon atom than the starting amide

questions.explanation: R-CONH₂ + Br₂ + 4 KOH → R-NH₂ + K₂CO₃ + 2 KBr + 2 H₂O. The carbonyl carbon is lost as carbonate.

questions.question: The Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction involves the halogenation of aliphatic carboxylic acids at which position in the presence of red phosphorus?
questions.explanation: R-CH₂-COOH + Cl₂ xrightarrow{red P} R-CH(Cl)-COOH + HCl (selective substitution of α-hydrogen).

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for oxalic acid (HOOC-COOH)?
questions.explanation: Oxalic acid has two carbons and two carboxylic groups: Ethanedioic acid.

questions.question: Which of the following dicarboxylic acids has three carbons (HOOC-CH₂-COOH) and yields acetic acid and CO₂ upon thermal decarboxylation?
questions.explanation: Malonic acid (propanedioic acid) readily decarboxylates at 150°C through a 6-membered cyclic transition state to form acetic acid and CO₂.

questions.question: The alkaline hydrolysis of fats and oils (triglycerides of long-chain fatty acids) with aqueous NaOH to form soap and glycerol is termed:
questions.explanation: Triglyceride + 3 NaOH → Glycerol + 3 R-COONa (soap molecules, e.g., sodium stearate).

questions.question: Which powerful reducing agent converts carboxylic acids directly into primary alcohols in high yield?

options.A: Lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH₄) in dry ether

questions.explanation: R-COOH xrightarrow{1. LiAlH₄/ether, 2. H₃O⁺} R-CH₂OH. NaBH₄ is not strong enough to reduce carboxylic acids.

questions.question: Formic acid (methanoic acid, HCOOH) differs from all other carboxylic acids because it contains both a carboxyl group and an aldehyde group (-CHO), allowing it to:

options.A: Reduce Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution to silver mirror and red Cu₂O

questions.explanation: H-COOH has an oxidizable formyl C-H bond, acting as a reducing agent that decolorizes KMnO₄ and reduces Tollens' reagent to metallic silver.

questions.question: Dehydration of acetic acid by heating with phosphorus pentoxide (P₂O₅) produces:
questions.explanation: 2 CH₃COOH xrightarrow{P₂O₅, \Delta} (CH₃CO)₂O + H₂O (intermolecular removal of water).

questions.question: When ammonium acetate (CH₃COONH₄) is heated dry, it loses a molecule of water to produce:
questions.explanation: CH₃COONH₄ xrightarrow{\Delta} CH₃CONH₂ (acetamide) + H₂O.

questions.question: Further dehydration of acetamide (CH₃CONH₂) with P₂O₅ produces:
questions.explanation: CH₃CONH₂ xrightarrow{P₂O₅, \Delta} CH₃-C≡N (acetonitrile) + H₂O.

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for Phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid)?
questions.explanation: Phthalic acid is ortho-benzene-dicarboxylic acid: Benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid.

questions.question: Heating phthalic acid causes intramolecular loss of water to form a crystalline cyclic anhydride called:
questions.explanation: Two adjacent carboxyl groups condense intramolecularly upon heating to form phthalic anhydride + H₂O.

questions.question: Which of the following acids is responsible for the sharp, stinging pain of ant bites and bee stings?
questions.explanation: Formic acid (from Latin formica, ant) is injected by venomous ants and bees into epidermal tissues.

questions.question: Vinegar is an aqueous solution containing approximately what percentage of acetic acid?
questions.explanation: Household vinegar is 4-8% ethanoic (acetic) acid in water, typically manufactured by oxidative fermentation of ethanol by Acetobacter aceti.

questions.question: Pure anhydrous acetic acid (freezing point 16.6°C) solidifies in winter into ice-like transparent crystals, earning it the name:
questions.explanation: Anhydrous acetic acid (100%) freezes into glittering glacier-like crystals at 16.6°C, hence termed glacial acetic acid.

questions.question: The pleasant fruity fragrance of ripe fruits, flavorings, and perfumes is primarily due to:

options.A: Esters (e.g., isoamyl acetate in bananas, ethyl butyrate in pineapples)

questions.explanation: Volatile aliphatic esters impart characteristic sweet fruit odors (e.g., banana, pineapple, apple, strawberry).

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for Adipic acid, a precursor for the manufacture of Nylon-6,6?
questions.explanation: Adipic acid has 6 carbons with terminal carboxyl groups: Hexanedioic acid.

questions.question: Why is benzoic acid a solid at room temperature (m.p. 122°C) while aliphatic carboxylic acids of similar carbon count (like heptanoic acid) are liquids?

options.A: Planar phenyl rings and strong hydrogen-bonded dimeric structures pack tightly into a rigid crystal lattice

questions.explanation: Planar aromatic rings facilitate dense crystal packing reinforced by centrosymmetric cyclic dimeric hydrogen bonds.

questions.question: Transesterification is the reaction between an ester and an alcohol in the presence of an acid or base catalyst, producing:

options.A: A new ester and a new alcohol

questions.explanation: R-COOR' + R''-OH ⇌ R-COOR'' + R'-OH; this alcoholysis is the core process in converting vegetable oils into biodiesel.

questions.question: Which of the following functional derivatives of carboxylic acids has the highest boiling point due to extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding involving two donor sites?
questions.explanation: Primary amides (-CONH₂) possess highly polar carbonyl and amino groups that form strong multi-directional hydrogen-bonded networks, resulting in unusually high melting and boiling points.

questions.question: Hydrolysis of an ester with aqueous mineral acid (e.g., dilute HCl) is reversible, whereas alkaline hydrolysis (saponification) is irreversible because:

options.A: The carboxylate anion formed is resonance-stabilized and unreactive toward nucleophilic attack by the weakly nucleophilic alcohol

questions.explanation: Deprotonation of carboxylic acid by OH⁻ produces carboxylate anion (RCOO⁻); negative charge repels nucleophiles, driving saponification to completion.

questions.question: When calcium formate [(HCOO)₂Ca] is heated alone, it yields:
questions.explanation: (HCOO)₂Ca xrightarrow{\Delta} HCHO + CaCO₃.

questions.question: Acid anhydrides react with water to produce:
questions.explanation: (RCO)₂O + H₂O → 2 R-COOH.

questions.question: Which acid is present in rancid butter, giving it an intensely repulsive odor?
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis of butterfat liberates free butanoic (butyric) acid, producing the characteristic foul smell of spoiled butter.

questions.question: Ammonolysis of an acyl chloride (RCOCl + 2 NH₃) yields:

options.A: An acid amide (RCONH₂) and ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl)

questions.explanation: R-COCl + 2 NH₃ → R-CONH₂ + NH₄Cl.

questions.question: What is the hybrid state of the carbonyl carbon in an ester?
questions.explanation: The ester carbonyl carbon is bonded to three atoms (=O, -OR, and -R) with 120° bond angles, hence sp² hybridized.

questions.question: Tartaric acid, found in tamarinds and grapes and used in baking powder, has the formula:
questions.explanation: Tartaric acid is 2,3-dihydroxybutanedioic acid, possessing two chiral centers and existing in d, l, and meso stereoisomers.

questions.question: Citric acid, found in citrus fruits like lemons and oranges, is a:

options.A: Tricarboxylic acid containing one hydroxyl group (2-hydroxypropane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid)

questions.explanation: Citric acid (C₆H₈O₇) has three -COOH groups and one tertiary -OH group: 2-hydroxypropane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid.

questions.question: Kolbe's electrolysis of an aqueous solution of sodium succinate yields which gaseous hydrocarbon at the anode?
questions.explanation: At the anode, succinate undergoes decarboxylation: -OOC-CH₂-CH₂-COO- - 2e⁻ → •CH₂-CH₂• + 2 CO₂ → H₂C=CH₂ (ethene) + 2 CO₂.
